title: ACS image of ESO 306-17
caption: The elliptical galaxy ESO 306-17, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: ESO 306-17 · constellation Columba · about 500 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This image from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys highlights the large, bright elliptical galaxy ESO 306-17 in the southern sky, about 500 million light-years away in the constellation Columba. It seems to be surrounded by other galaxies, but the bright ones at bottom left are thought to lie in the foreground rather than at the same distance.

In fact, ESO 306-17 sits largely on its own, surrounded by a vast expanse of hot gas and dark matter. It belongs to what astronomers call a fossil group, a very different setting from a crowded cluster of galaxies.

Researchers are also using the Hubble data to hunt for nearby ultra-compact dwarf galaxies. These are miniature dwarfs stripped down to little more than their cores by encounters with larger, more powerful galaxies. Most found so far sit near giant ellipticals in large galaxy clusters, so researchers want to know whether similar objects also turn up in a fossil group like this one.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.21 x 3.19 arcminutes) and distance (500 million light years), the frame spans roughly 467,000 × 464,000 light-years. Its light set out about 500 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys observed through blue and near-infrared filters, with a synthetic green channel. The colour mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Long exposures and near-infrared light reveal faint galaxies the eye couldn't see.
